basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 5.' and it opens '| Vers. 5. Percusserunt Raphaim. Id est gigantes, qui Raphaim gigantes interpretatur.'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: | Vers. 5. Percusserunt Raphaim. Id est gigantes, qui Raphaim gigantes interpretatur. Carnaim et Guttim [Vulg., Zuzim ] nomina locorum sunt et gentium. Seir per prolepsin dicitur, necdum enim locus ille sic vocabatur. Seir ipse est Edom, qui et Esau interpretatur hispidus, setosus, qui in modum pellis natus est, a quo regio quam possedit Seir vocata es
